summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old man with a history of alcohol use disorder, alcoholic cirrhosis, and opioid use disorder was admitted for alcohol withdrawal after relapsing and consuming large amounts of vodka daily for six days. He presented with tremors, abdominal pain, vomiting with blood streaks, visual disturbances, and altered mental status. He was managed with a phenobarbital taper in the ICU, transitioned to the general floor, and completed detoxification. Hepatic encephalopathy was treated with lactulose and rifaximin, with improvement in mental status. Hepatopulmonary syndrome was diagnosed via echocardiogram and confirmed on CT angiogram, but oxygen levels improved with activity, avoiding home oxygen. Pancytopenia and portal hypertension were noted on imaging and labs, with no acute bleeding. He was restarted on buprenorphine, received hepatitis vaccinations, and was discharged home with plans for a dual diagnosis day program, follow-up with hepatology, and strict alcohol abstinence.
problems: Alcoholic cirrhosis of liver without ascites
